channel.title: EnergySavers: News
channel.description: The latest UK energy and water bill news explained: price cap changes, the Budget, VAT, supplier takeovers, grants and new rules, with what each means for you.

item.title: Autumn Budget 2026: what to watch for energy bills
item.description: The Autumn Budget is on 28 October 2026. What has been reported on energy bill support and levies, what’s already confirmed, and what it could mean for you.

item.title: Should you fix your energy this winter?
item.description: With the January 2027 price cap forecast to rise, should you fix your gas and electricity? How to weigh fixes against the cap, exit fees and the VAT change.

item.title: Landlords and EPC C by 2030: what’s been decided
item.description: Private landlords in England and Wales must reach EPC C by 1 October 2030. The confirmed rules, the £10,000 cost cap, exemptions and what renters can expect.

item.title: E.ON and OVO takeover: what it means for you
item.description: E.ON is buying OVO after competition clearance in October 2026. What happens to OVO tariffs, credit, direct debits and switching while the deal completes.

item.title: Water bills in 2026 and the end of Ofwat
item.description: Why water bills rose in April 2026, what replacing Ofwat with a new regulator means for customers, and the help available if you’re struggling to pay.

item.title: Warm Home Discount 2026/27: who gets £150?
item.description: The £150 Warm Home Discount has reopened for winter 2026 to 2027. Who qualifies in England, Wales and Scotland, how it’s paid and other help to claim.

item.title: 0% VAT on electricity: what it means for your bill
item.description: VAT on household electricity in Great Britain is 0% from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. Who gets it, whether fixed tariffs are covered and what happens next.

item.title: October 2026 price cap: what’s changed and why
item.description: The energy price cap rose 4% to £1,723 on 1 October 2026. Here are the new rates, why gas prices rose, how the VAT cut changes things and what to do now.
